messages:
elin.design: Quick sync: prototyped a new modal footer layout for multi-action flows (confirm + secondary + help). Wanted quick gut check on CTA ordering, spacing, and mobile stacking.
kai.engineering: can you drop the figma link? :eyes:
elin.design: https://figma.com/file/efgh/modal-footer-proposals — Proposal A keeps primary right, secondary left; Proposal B stacks primary above secondary on mobile. I also tightened horizontal padding using `--space-3` -> `--space-2`.
pat.pm: for destructive flows we need primary to be more prominent. If primary is destructive, maybe we invert styling (primary -> red) but keep positional rules consistent.
ria.a11y: a couple a11y points: 1) tabbable order must follow visual order when stacked. 2) if primary changes color for destructive, ensure 3:1 contrast against background for small text buttons.
kai.engineering: stacking behavior idea: on narrow widths switch to column-reverse so primary ends up first in tab order by default. CSS: 

```css
.modal-footer { display: flex; gap: var(--space-2); padding: var(--space-3); justify-content: flex-end; }
@media (max-width: 520px) { .modal-footer { flex-direction: column-reverse; align-items: stretch; } }
```

That keeps primary visually on top on mobile and last in DOM when we use column-reverse. But need to confirm keyboard order.
elin.design: hmm that could be surprising for screen reader users if DOM order != visual order. Ria, prefer DOM match visual?
ria.a11y: Yes, DOM should match visual order. column-reverse flips visual order but not DOM. Better approach: change DOM order via JS or render order for mobile. Or use `order` on flex children with careful tabindex management. Simpler: render primary last on desktop, on mobile re-render with primary as first child.
pat.pm: re-rendering sounds fine if we keep markup simple and avoid focus traps. Also add `aria-describedby` when we show help link to provide context.
elin.design: OK. Also testing note: we tightened spacing tokens; will that break layouts elsewhere? Kai, you mentioned token audit earlier.
kai.engineering: will run `yarn tokens:diff` and grep for `--space-2` changes. If any modal-specific tokens are used globally we may need a dedicated `--modal-padding` token.
ria.a11y: tiny nit: when stacking, ensure the primary button still meets 44x44 touch target and has at least 8px between buttons to avoid mis-taps.
elin.design: good call. I'll update the spec: `--space-2` -> 8px gap min, primary height = 44px on touch. Also adding a visual cue: subtle divider above footer `box-shadow: inset 0 1px var(--muted-200)`.
pat.pm: decision? We should pick one for v1: Desktop: primary on right, secondary left; Mobile: re-render DOM so primary appears first and stacked above. Add modal-specific tokens and a11y checklist.
kai.engineering: implementable. I'll include a small helper in react-modal: `<Footer primaryFirstOnMobile />` and switch render order based on `useMediaQuery`. Will include unit test for DOM order.
ria.a11y: I'll add accessibility test to axe check: tab order, contrast, touch target.
ux-bot: Reminder: create a release note entry under UI changes for modal footer behavior.
elin.design: Thanks team. I'll update Figma frames, add the modal token (`--modal-padding`, `--modal-footer-gap`), and open a PR with screenshots. Assigning to @kai for implementation and @ria for final a11y signoff. :thumbsup:
